day-1.t: Day 1 — What React is and your first component

b.v: Today's goal

v: Know what React does
Write a component
Run it right here in the lesson

b.v: About 25 minutes. Finish the JavaScript course first – React is JavaScript.

React is a JavaScript library for building user interfaces. You split the screen into small pieces called components – a button, a card, a whole page – and React keeps the screen in step with your data. Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp Web are built with it.
1) A component is a function that returns what to show
Press Run. Then change the text and press Run again. The lines at the top load React; you only edit the part in the middle.
2) Components inside components

v: A component name starts with a capital letter (Greeting, not greeting)
It returns JSX – HTML-like code inside JavaScript
You use it like a tag: <Greeting />

b.v: These examples load React from the internet. If Run shows nothing, check your connection and press Run again.
Today's goal

v: Write JSX without errors
Put JavaScript values inside JSX
Know where JSX differs from HTML

b.v: About 25 minutes.
1) The five rules

v: Return one parent element – wrap siblings in a <div> or in <> </>
Close every tag, even and
Use className instead of class
Put JavaScript inside { } – values, maths, function calls
Style is an object: style={{ color: "red", fontSize: 20 }}

b.v: You cannot write if or for directly inside JSX. Use the ternary a ? b : c, or && , or work it out above the return.

day-3.t: Day 3 — Props: passing data to components

b.v: Today's goal

v: Pass values into a component
Reuse one component with different data
Pass children

b.v: About 25 minutes.
Props are the inputs of a component, like the arguments of a function. A parent passes them; the child reads them and never changes them.
1) children
Numbers and true/false go in braces: lessons={10}. Plain text can use quotes: name="React".
Today's goal

v: Make a component remember a value
Update the screen by changing state
Avoid the common state mistakes

b.v: About 30 minutes.
State is data a component remembers between renders. When you change it with its setter, React draws the component again with the new value.

v: const [value, setValue] = useState(start) = make a state variable
Call setValue(newValue) to change it – never value = ...
Each component on the screen has its own copy of its state

b.v: 1) Objects and arrays: make a new copy
user.city = 'Karachi' changes the object but React does not notice, so the screen does not update. Always pass a new object or array to the setter.
Today's goal

v: Handle clicks and typing
Build a controlled input
Stop the page reloading on submit

b.v: About 30 minutes.

v: onClick, onChange, onSubmit = event props, written in camelCase
Pass a function – onClick={save} – not the result of calling it – onClick={save()}
Controlled input = value comes from state and onChange updates the state
e.preventDefault() = stops the browser's normal form submit

b.v: Controlled inputs make validation easy: the button above stays disabled until the name is long enough.

day-6.t: Day 6 — Lists, keys and showing things conditionally

b.v: Today's goal

v: Turn an array into a list on screen
Use keys correctly
Filter what is shown

b.v: About 30 minutes.

v: array.map(...) = one element for each item
key = a stable, unique id so React can track each row
array.filter(...) = show only some items

condition &&

…

= show only when the condition is true

b.v: Don't use the array index as the key when items can be added, removed or re-ordered. Use the item's id.
Today's goal

v: Run code after the component appears
Load data with loading and error states
Clean up timers

b.v: About 30 minutes.
useEffect runs code after React has drawn the screen – to load data, start a timer or talk to the browser. The list at the end (the dependency array) says when to run it again.
1) Real fetch looks like this
2) Cleaning up

v: useEffect(fn, []) = run once
useEffect(fn, [a]) = run when a changes
No array at all = run after every render (rarely what you want)
Return a function to clean up timers and listeners

day-8.t: Day 8 — Sharing state and your own hooks

b.v: Today's goal

v: Lift state up to a parent
Pass functions down as props
Write a custom hook

b.v: About 30 minutes.
When two components need the same data, keep it in their closest common parent and pass it down. Children change it by calling a function the parent gives them.
1) A custom hook
A custom hook is a function starting with use that bundles state and effects so you can reuse them.
Call hooks only at the top level of a component or another hook – never inside if, loops or ordinary functions.

day-9.t: Day 9 — A real project on your computer with Vite

b.v: Today's goal

v: Create a React project on your own computer
Know the folder structure
Build it for a live site

b.v: About 30 minutes. You need Node.js (the LTS version from nodejs.org).

@Terminal
npm create vite@latest my-app -- --template react
cd my-app
npm install
npm run dev
Open the address it prints (usually http://localhost:5173). Edit src/App.jsx, save, and the page updates by itself.

v: index.html = the one HTML page
src/main.jsx = starts React and renders <App />
src/App.jsx = your main component
package.json = the project's packages and scripts
node_modules = installed packages – never edit, never upload to GitHub

b.v: 1) Files and imports
2) Build for a live site
The dist folder can be served by Nginx, or by free hosts such as Netlify or Vercel. In the live project you serve it next to your Django API.
